   - Removed the declaration of the variable `id` from the function `lpfc_nvmet_xmt_fcp_op` and instead declared it within the scope of the `if` statement that checks for `CONFIG_SCSI_LPFC_DEBUG_FS`. This change prevents the unused variable warning when debugfs support is not enabled.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `lpfc_debugfs.h` and `lpfc_nvmet.c` are interrelated as they both address issues arising from the absence of debugfs support. The changes in `lpfc_debugfs.h` ensure that necessary identifiers and macros are conditionally defined based on the presence of debugfs support, which resolves the compilation errors related to undeclared identifiers in `lpfc_nvmet.c`. Additionally, the adjustment in `lpfc_nvmet.c` to declare the variable `id` only when needed prevents warnings about unused variables, thus improving the overall code quality and maintainability when debugfs support is not available.

content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the presence of undeclared identifiers (`DUMP_FCP` and `DUMP_NVME`) and an implicit declaration of the function `lpfc_nvmeio_data` in the `lpfc_nvmet.c` file when building without debugfs support. This occurred because the enumeration defining these identifiers was moved to a conditional compilation block that is only included when `CONFIG_SCSI_LPFC_DEBUG_FS` is defined, leading to compilation failures when debugfs support is not enabled.
        
        Commit message:
        scsi: lpfc: fix building without debugfs support

On a randconfig build without CONFIG_SCSI_LPFC_DEBUG_FS, I ran into
multiple compile failures:

drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_debugfs.h: In function 'lpfc_debug_dump_wq':
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_debugfs.h:405:15: error: 'DUMP_FCP' undeclared (first use in this function); did you mean 'DUMP_VAR'?
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_debugfs.h:405:15: note: each undeclared identifier is reported only once for each function it appears in
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_debugfs.h:408:22: error: 'DUMP_NVME' undeclared (first use in this function); did you mean 'DUMP_NONE'?
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvmet.c: In function 'lpfc_nvmet_xmt_ls_rsp_cmp':
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvmet.c:109:2: error: implicit declaration of function 'lpfc_nvmeio_data'; did you mean 'lpfc_mem_free'? [-Werror=implicit-function-declaration]
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvmet.c: In function 'lpfc_nvmet_xmt_fcp_op':
drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvmet.c:523:10: error: unused variable 'id' [-Werror=unused-variable]

They are all trivial to fix, so I'm doing it in a combined patch here.

Fixes: 1d9d5a9879ad ("scsi: lpfc: refactor debugfs queue dump routines")
Fixes: bd2cdd5e400f ("scsi: lpfc: NVME Initiator: Add debugfs support")
Fixes: 2b65e18202fd ("scsi: lpfc: NVME Target: Add debugfs support")
Signed-off-by: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Acked-by: Dick Kennedy <dick.kennedy@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>
